topic: Your sunroof stopped mid-slide? Here's why it might not close.
negativePromptStanding: faces, hands, human figures, on-screen text, logos, watermarks, subtitles

beats.label: HOOK
beats.narration: Your sunroof stopped halfway — won't slide open or closed?
beats.visualPrompt: Interior shot looking up at a sunroof panel stopped partway open, headliner and sunroof frame visible, soft cabin light, static-mounted camera, slight push-in.

beats.label: SYMPTOM
beats.narration: Not leaking, not loose — just stuck. That's a different problem.
beats.visualPrompt: Close macro on the sunroof track edge, subtle dust/grime texture visible along the rail, shallow depth of field.

beats.label: EXPLANATION
beats.narration: One clue: dirt or dried lubricant on the track can make it bind — a simple clean and re-grease.
beats.visualPrompt: Macro/cutaway shot: an inspection light angled along the track, revealing dried lubricant residue and light debris buildup in contrast light; slow rack focus from clean rail to grimy rail.

beats.label: CONSEQUENCE
beats.narration: But if it's the motor — worn out or a stripped gear — that's not a cleaning job.
beats.visualPrompt: Cutaway to a sunroof motor/drive-gear assembly (generic automotive part, no badge/logo), soft workshop lighting, subtle rotation-stall motion.

beats.label: SAFE_ACTION
beats.narration: Don't force it. Forcing a stuck sunroof can turn a cheap fix into an expensive one.
beats.visualPrompt: Interior shot again, sunroof panel static in its stuck position, brief pull-back to show full headliner context, calm and steady camera.

beats.label: BRANDED_CTA
beats.narration: Worth checking either way. Stop by and we'll take a look. Nick's Tire & Auto.
beats.visualPrompt: Branded end-card plate: Nick's Tire & Auto shop bay wide shot, warm daylight, static hold. Logo/CTA text composited in post, not generated.
